FAQ.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQ.paragraph: We have answered the most common questions, related with registrations, please feel free to

questions_list.question: Do I need a subscription to become a member?
questions_list.answer: A subscription to IEEE is not mandatory to participate in our teams. However, members with a subscription enjoy significant benefits, such as priority access to events with limited spots and participation in official IEEE competitions, among many others.

questions_list.question: Must I actively participate in a scientific group/project?
questions_list.answer: Our goal is to create an active community. For this reason, we encourage every member to be part of at least one team and actively participate in one of its projects and figure out their schedule with the appropriate team leader or project manager.

questions_list.question: Is any previous knowledge/experience required or can I learn through participating?
questions_list.answer: There are no prior knowledge requirements to join the Student Branch. However, team leaders or project managers may define specific skill or knowledge prerequisites for certain projects to ensure effective organization and successful outcomes.

questions_list.question: How much time do I need to devote?
questions_list.answer: The time required depends on how many projects you participate in and the demands of each project. However, in most cases, dedicating just a few hours per week is sufficient.

questions_list.question: Do I need to be an electrical or electronics engineer in order to participate?
questions_list.answer: No! The Student Branch is open to everyone, even non-engineers. In addition to the scientific groups, there are many other teams that manage important aspects of the Student Branch that are unrelated to engineering. You can get involved with these teams after discussing them through the registration process.

questions_list.question: Must you be a student to be a part of the branch?
questions_list.answer: No. Although most members are usually undergraduates, mostly due to more free time, there is no limit to who can participate in our teams or attend our events.

IEEE.title: What is the IEEE?
IEEE.caption: The world's largest technological organization
IEEE.text: The Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE) is the world's largest technical professional organization, focused on advancing technology for the benefit of humanity.
bulletedList: It was founded in 1963 through the merger of the American Institute of Electrical Engineers and the Institute of Radio Engineers.
The organization's headquarters are located in New York.
It is the largest organization of technology professionals, with approximately 430,000 members in around 160 countries.
The majority of members are engineers and scientists/academics. Most of them are computer scientists, software engineers, IT professionals, physicists, and even doctors.
For this reason, the organization often prefers using the acronym IEEE rather than its full name.

IEEEStudents.title: What is an IEEE Student Branch?
IEEEStudents.caption: University-based IEEE Community
IEEEStudents.text: An IEEE Student Branch (SB) is a local unit of IEEE established within a university, designed to engage students in fields related to IEEE’s mission. The main objective of an SB is to foster connections among students—both within the university and with other IEEE Student Branches globally—as well as with industry professionals. These connections promote education, innovation, and technical development through collaboration and exposure to real-world challenges and solutions. Student Branches actively organize a variety of activities, including technical workshops, seminars, competitions, and project development. Many of these initiatives are eligible for funding and support through IEEE, helping to enrich the student experience and bridge the gap between academia and industry. Like the broader IEEE organization, an SB can also establish and host both technical societies and affinity groups that mirror IEEE’s official structure. These groups serve as a direct link to their parent IEEE entities and can be used to organize targeted events, receive funding, and pursue the specific goals and missions of each society or affinity group.

IEEEGreeceSection.title: What is the Greece Section?
IEEEGreeceSection.caption: IEEE Community in Greece
IEEEGreeceSection.text: The IEEE Greece Section is the national branch of IEEE in Greece and operates as part of IEEE Region 8. It serves IEEE members throughout the country, contributing to the advancement of technology and engineering both locally and within the global IEEE community. As a central hub for Greek universities, the IEEE Greece Section fosters collaboration among academia, industry, and research organizations. It plays a vital role in facilitating the exchange of technical knowledge and innovative ideas across these sectors.

IEEERegion8.title: What is the IEEE Region 8?
IEEERegion8.caption: An IEEE Network – From Europe to Africa!
IEEERegion8.text: IEEE Region 8 is one of the 10 geographical regions of the IEEE. It includes Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA). The region encompasses a diverse range of countries and cultures, and it plays a vital role in the development and advancement of engineering, technology, and innovation across these areas. The IEEE Region 8 Student Activities Committee (R8 SAC), one of the many committees of the region, is responsible for student initiatives, events and competitions held within the region.
